title: Online shopping
subtitle: basket, delivery, reviews, post code
summary: Buy things on a website: search, read reviews, add to your basket, pay and wait for the delivery.

lesson.heading: Buying something on a website
lesson.text: First you **search** for the product you want. The website shows the **colour**, the **size** and the **price**. When you want it, you click **Add to basket**. Your **basket** holds everything you are going to buy.

examples.text: Cotton T-shirt. **Colour**: white, blue or red. **Size**: small, medium or large.
**Reading** the **reviews** can help you choose what to buy.
examples.note: a review = what other buyers say about a product

lesson.heading: Delivery options
lesson.note: If you are not at home to receive the delivery, they take it to the post office.

lesson.heading: Your order
lesson.text: When you pay, the website gives your **order** an **order number**. You can still **delete** an item from your basket before you pay. The **total** is all the money together.

examples.text: I don't want the blue one. I'll **delete this item**.

lesson.heading: Post code
lesson.text: A **post code** is a short code at the end of an address. In the UK it has letters and numbers, for example BA1 1LZ. In the US it is called a **zip code** and it is only numbers, for example 10509.

lesson.heading: Talking about online shopping
lesson.text: We **shop online** because it is quick and easy. Most people **pay with** a **credit card**.

examples.text: Lisa likes to **shop online** because it's quick and easy.
Most people **pay for** their online shopping **with credit cards**.

lesson.text: We put something in our basket, but we never say ~~a shopping bag~~ for this on a website - the word is always basket.

exercises.prompt: Match the words with the examples.
When you shop online, you can ___ for the best price.
exercises.explanation: You search a website for the product and the price you want.

exercises.prompt: You can read ___ from other people who bought the same thing.
exercises.explanation: A review says what a buyer thinks of a product.

exercises.prompt: If you want to buy something, ___ it to your basket.
exercises.explanation: We add an item to our basket.

exercises.prompt: If you don't want to buy something that is in your basket, you can ___ it.
exercises.explanation: You delete an item to take it out of your basket.

exercises.prompt: You can use your ___ to pay for your shopping.
exercises.explanation: Most people pay for their online shopping with a credit card.
Every order gets an order number, so the shop can find it.

exercises.prompt: *Customer care:* And what's your address and ___? *Tom:* 31 Mill Road, WC2 5SN.
exercises.explanation: In the UK the post code has letters and numbers.

exercises.prompt: I paid £5 for ___ delivery, so my shoes will be here tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Next day delivery costs more, but it arrives tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: You are buying a computer online. Match each step to the right place in the order.

pairs.right: Read online reviews and choose which computer to buy
Search for a website which sells that computer
Add the computer to your basket
Wait at home for the delivery

exercises.statement: A post code in the UK has letters and numbers, for example BA1 1LZ.
exercises.explanation: Correct. A US zip code has only numbers, for example 10509.

exercises.prompt: Does the website ask for this in your order, or in your delivery address?

exercises.answer: Lisa likes to shop online because it's quick and easy.
exercises.explanation: We shop online - no preposition after online.
